title: {name} and the Humming Bridge
text:
On a golden autumn afternoon, Sora unfolded her map on a flat rock beside the winding path. {name} leaned in close to look. Sora tapped one small mark with her finger. "The old stone bridge," she said. "That is where the moss hums."

Ravi came bouncing down the path to join them, making up a silly song about the map, with a silly verse about a frog who could not read. Sora counted her steps out loud and never lost her place.

Just then, something tumbled out from under a fern. It was Pippa, in her red acorn cap, blinking up at them. Ravi sang her right into his song, and Pippa squeaked along in her tiny voice, a little bit off the tune.

At a fork in the path, Sora stopped and turned her map one way, then the other. "The map says left," she said, "but the path goes right." Pippa sniffed the air. The way to the right smelled of warm berries, so they followed her nose.

The path ended at the old stone bridge, just as the light turned deep amber. Ravi's song grew slower, and slower, until it was only a hum. The lanterns dim, and the forest grows hushed.

Sora tucked her map into her big pocket. Then {name}, Sora and Ravi lay on their tummies and pressed their ears to the soft moss at the end of the bridge. And the moss hummed back, very softly, in Ravi's own tune. Nobody said a word.

When the first stars peeked out, Bramble came along the brook path with his small lantern. "Come along, little ones," he said softly. "It is time to settle down." Ravi hummed the tune again, and yawned right in the middle of it. The lanterns dim, and the forest grows hushed.

At the end of the path, a bed of soft moss was waiting. {name} curled up on it, and Pippa, who had trotted along all the way, tucked in close. The humming was still there, very faintly, like a lullaby the whole forest knew. {Subject} smiled, and drifted off to sleep. The lanterns dim, and the forest grows hushed.
